text: [TRUE] With this sign you must adjust speed to the particular conditions of the road surface.
[TRUE] Reducing speed avoids excessive stress and damage to the suspension on the irregular surface.
[TRUE] You must hold the steering wheel firmly to control possible swerving on the uneven surface.
[FALSE] There is no obligation to drive in the centre of the carriageway; you should keep right and slow down.
[FALSE] The sign warns of uneven road, not of a narrowing carriageway, which has its own sign.
[FALSE] You must slow down regardless of oncoming traffic, to protect the vehicle and keep control.
[TRUE] Because visibility beyond the crest is limited, speed must be moderated in relation to what you can see.
[TRUE] U-turns are prohibited on a dosso because of the limited visibility.
[TRUE] On a dosso both parking (sosta) and stopping (fermata) are prohibited on the uphill and downhill stretches.
[FALSE] It is a danger sign; it does not prohibit the transit of buses or any other vehicle category.
[FALSE] The overtaking ban applies to the uphill stretch, where visibility is limited by the crest, not to the downhill stretch.
[FALSE] U-turns are prohibited on the whole dosso stretch, including the downhill part.
[TRUE] Speed must be moderated on a dip to avoid damage to the suspension.
[TRUE] Moderating speed helps maintain control of the vehicle through the dip.
[TRUE] In case of rain, water can accumulate in the dip, and this must be anticipated.
[FALSE] You must slow down through a dip regardless of oncoming traffic.
[FALSE] You must slow down even if the dip is visible, to protect the suspension and keep control.
[FALSE] The sign does not prohibit overtaking; on a one-way road there is no oncoming traffic, so this claimed prohibition does not apply.
[TRUE] Speed must be adjusted to visibility and to the radius of the bend.
[TRUE] On a wet road, grip is reduced, so the bend must be negotiated with extra care.
[TRUE] On a two-way carriageway with only two lanes, overtaking on the bend is prohibited due to limited visibility.
[FALSE] On a dangerous bend both parking (sosta) and stopping (fermata) are prohibited due to limited visibility.
[FALSE] U-turns are prohibited on dangerous bends due to limited visibility.
[FALSE] Reversing manoeuvres are prohibited on dangerous bends.
[TRUE] On a two-lane, two-way road, in the presence of the double bend sign you must drive as close as possible to the right-hand edge to reduce conflict with oncoming traffic.
[TRUE] In rain the road is slippery and grip is reduced, so the bends must be negotiated with extra care and lower speed.
[TRUE] The vehicle's load affects braking distance and cornering stability, so speed must be adjusted to load conditions.
[FALSE] The sign warns of dangerous bends, where U-turns (inversione di marcia) are prohibited, not allowed.
[FALSE] The sign warns of dangerous bends, where reversing (retromarcia) is prohibited, not permitted.
[FALSE] On bends with limited visibility both stopping (fermata) and parking (sosta) are prohibited.
[TRUE] In its presence you must slow down so as to be ready to stop safely if the barriers are closed.
[TRUE] If heavy traffic prevents you from clearing the crossing completely, you must not enter it, to avoid being trapped on the tracks.
[TRUE] Two alternately flashing red lights mean a train is approaching; you must stop and wait.
[FALSE] Parking (sosta) and stopping (fermata) are prohibited at and near level crossings.
[FALSE] You must slow down whenever this sign is present, not only in poor visibility, so you are always ready for closing barriers or red lights.
[FALSE] Both stopping (fermata) and parking (sosta) are prohibited at and near the tracks.
[TRUE] You must slow down in relation to how well you can see the railway line: the poorer the visibility, the lower the speed.
[TRUE] An un-barriered crossing has no physical protection, so you must proceed with the utmost caution, checking for trains in both directions.
[FALSE] You must slow down whenever this sign is present, not only in fog.
[FALSE] There is no obligation to sound the horn before crossing the tracks; the requirement is to slow down, look both ways and cross with caution.
[TRUE] The sign is the St Andrew's cross (CROCE DI S. ANDREA): a single red X indicating the railway line has only one track.
[TRUE] The St Andrew's cross is placed in the immediate vicinity of a level crossing without barriers, marking its exact position.
[TRUE] Along the road, the St Andrew's cross comes after the LEVEL CROSSING WITHOUT BARRIERS warning sign (about 150 m ahead) and stands just before the tracks.
[FALSE] The St Andrew's cross is installed only at crossings without barriers, never at crossings with half-barriers.
[FALSE] Below the St Andrew's cross there may be two alternately flashing red lights when a train approaches — never a green light.
[FALSE] The St Andrew's cross stands immediately by the tracks; the sign 150 metres away is the advance warning sign with the three-red-bar distance panel.
[TRUE] The double St Andrew's cross requires you to stop within the stop line (striscia di arresto) if a train is approaching.
[TRUE] The double St Andrew's cross is placed in the immediate vicinity of a level crossing without barriers.
[TRUE] The double St Andrew's cross (two superimposed crosses) indicates the railway line has more than one track.
[FALSE] The double St Andrew's cross stands immediately by the tracks; the sign about 150 m away is the advance warning sign with distance panel.
[FALSE] The double St Andrew's cross marks a multi-track railway crossing without barriers, not two consecutive road junctions.
[FALSE] The double St Andrew's cross is installed only at crossings without barriers, never at crossings with half-barriers.
[TRUE] Overtaking a moving tram on the right is one of the few cases where passing on the right is allowed, provided there is enough space.
[TRUE] You may drive on the tram tracks as long as you do not obstruct the tram's movement.
[TRUE] You may overtake on the right a tram stopped in the middle of the road for boarding/alighting only if there is a dedicated passenger refuge island (salvagente).
[FALSE] The sign does not prohibit overtaking trams for any vehicle category, let alone only motorcycles.
[FALSE] Driving over the tram tracks is allowed, provided you do not obstruct the tram.
[FALSE] Overtaking a tram is not restricted to the left: a moving tram may also be overtaken on the right when there is enough space.
[TRUE] The sign is the pedestrian crossing warning (attraversamento pedonale), announcing a zebra-striped crossing ahead.
[TRUE] Drivers must give way (dare la precedenza) to pedestrians crossing on the zebra stripes.
[TRUE] The sign entails the prohibition of overtaking a vehicle that has stopped to let pedestrians cross, so as not to endanger them.
[FALSE] The sign warns of a pedestrian crossing, not of a pedestrian promenade (viale pedonale).
[FALSE] You must not use the horn to make pedestrians move; the correct behaviour is to slow down and give way to them.
[FALSE] Stopping (fermata) and parking (sosta) on the pedestrian crossing are prohibited, regardless of the space left for pedestrians.
[TRUE] You must not overtake vehicles slowing down or stopping to let pedestrians cross, so as not to endanger the pedestrians.
[TRUE] In its presence you must slow down, ready to stop if pedestrians are crossing the carriageway.
[TRUE] Parking (sosta) and stopping (fermata) on the zebra stripes are prohibited.
[FALSE] You must not sound the horn at crossing pedestrians; the correct behaviour is to slow down and give way.
[FALSE] On the zebra stripes it is the vehicles that must give way to pedestrians, not the other way round.
[FALSE] Giving way to pedestrians on the stripes is mandatory; failing to do so carries fines and licence-point deductions.
[TRUE] In its presence you must drive so as not to create danger or obstruction for cyclists crossing the road.
[TRUE] You must slow down and be ready to stop to give way to cyclists who are crossing.
[TRUE] Overtaking a vehicle that has stopped to let cyclists cross is forbidden, as it would seriously endanger the crossing cyclists.
[FALSE] You must not sound the horn; you must slow down, stop if necessary and give way — the horn could frighten the cyclists.
[FALSE] At a cycle crossing it is the vehicles that must give way to crossing cyclists, not the other way round.
[FALSE] You must give way to all cyclists who are crossing, from either direction, not only those coming from the right.
[TRUE] On a descent vehicles tend to pick up speed, so you must slow down to avoid rear-ending slower vehicles ahead.
[TRUE] Prolonged braking overheats the brakes and can cause them to fade; use a low gear to control speed instead.
[TRUE] On a wet road braking distances on a descent increase significantly, so great caution is needed.
[FALSE] Continuous braking overheats the brakes; the correct technique is a low gear and engine braking, not constant braking to spare the gearbox.
[FALSE] Driving with the clutch depressed eliminates engine braking and is dangerous; engage a suitably low gear.
[FALSE] Braking distances increase on a descent, so you must increase (not reduce) the safety distance from the vehicle ahead.
[TRUE] It warns of a climb (10% gradient) to be driven with particular caution.
[TRUE] On a steep climb you must engage a suitably low gear so the engine delivers enough power.
[FALSE] Tight bends are warned by bend signs; this sign warns of a steep 10% climb.
[FALSE] The wedge rises left-to-right, indicating a climb; a descent is shown by the descending wedge of the discesa pericolosa sign.
[TRUE] It warns of a narrow passage where passing vehicles coming from the opposite direction may be difficult.
[TRUE] The symbol narrows on both sides, indicating the carriageway narrows on both the left and the right.
[TRUE] Since the carriageway narrows ahead, you must moderate your speed and, if needed, stop to let oncoming vehicles through.
[FALSE] It only warns of a narrowing; the obligation to give way in alternating one-way traffic is imposed by the separate 'dare precedenza' sign, not by this one.
[FALSE] It does not grant priority over oncoming traffic; that is conveyed by the blue 'diritto di precedenza' sign.
[FALSE] It warns of a narrowing of the carriageway, not of a tunnel entrance.
[TRUE] The skidding-car symbol is the slippery road (strada sdrucciolevole) sign; it warns of a stretch that becomes dangerous in the weather conditions specified by supplementary panels.
[TRUE] On a slippery surface tyre grip can decrease, which is exactly the hazard this sign warns of.
[TRUE] The sign requires moderate speed and avoiding sudden manoeuvres such as sharp braking, acceleration or steering.
[FALSE] Strong side wind is warned by the windsock sign; this sign warns of a slippery road surface.
[FALSE] On a slippery road braking distance increases, not decreases, because tyre grip is reduced.
[FALSE] A road with many curves is warned by bend signs; the skidding-car symbol indicates a slippery road.
[TRUE] In rain the slippery surface reduces grip, so you must moderate speed and avoid sudden braking to prevent skidding.
[TRUE] On ice the surface is extremely slippery, so you must moderate speed and avoid sudden acceleration to prevent wheelspin.
[FALSE] In rain you must increase, not decrease, the distance from the vehicle ahead, to compensate for longer braking distances.
[FALSE] The obligation to fit snow chains is imposed by a dedicated mandatory sign; this is only a slippery-road warning sign.
[TRUE] In its presence you must pay particular attention to the possible presence of children near or on the road.
[TRUE] Children's movements are unpredictable, so pay particular attention and be ready to stop.
[TRUE] Overtaking a vehicle that has stopped to let children cross is prohibited, as it would seriously endanger the crossing children.
[FALSE] Attention is required for children on the sidewalk too, since they may suddenly run onto the carriageway.
[FALSE] It is a warning sign; transit is never prohibited, you only must slow down and pay attention.
[FALSE] The sign imposes no specific speed limit such as 30 km/h; it only requires moderate speed and caution.
[TRUE] The sign (doppio senso di circolazione), with one up and one down arrow, warns that a one-way carriageway is about to become two-way.
[TRUE] Once one-way traffic ends you may meet vehicles travelling in the opposite direction, so greater caution is required.
[TRUE] On a two-way stretch overtaking (sorpasso), where permitted, must be carried out with particular caution because of oncoming traffic.
[FALSE] It is the opposite: traffic changes from one-way to two-way (doppio senso), not the other way round.
[FALSE] Giving way to oncoming vehicles belongs to the alternating one-way precedence signs; this is only a danger warning sign.
[FALSE] An alternating one-way section (senso unico alternato) is announced by its own specific sign; this sign announces two-way traffic.
[TRUE] The sign (materiale instabile sulla strada) warns of loose gravel on the surface, where the vehicle's grip (aderenza) can decrease.
[TRUE] Gravel can be thrown sideways by passing vehicles, so caution is required toward pedestrians even off the carriageway.
[TRUE] On loose gravel grip decreases, so the danger of skidding or slipping (sbandamento/slittamento) must be taken into account.
[FALSE] Landslide/rockfall danger is announced by the falling-rocks sign (caduta massi); this sign warns of loose gravel on the surface.
[FALSE] Soft shoulders are announced by the banchina pericolosa sign; this sign concerns loose gravel on the pavement.
[FALSE] Falling rocks are announced by the caduta massi sign; this sign concerns gravel already lying on the road surface.
[TRUE] The rock face drawn on the right side of the sign warns of rocks falling from the right (caduta massi da destra).
[TRUE] Fallen rocks remain on the carriageway, so the sign warns of stones possibly lying on the road.
[TRUE] Moderating speed helps avoid hitting rocks that have fallen onto the carriageway.
[FALSE] A narrowing on the right (strettoia) has its own sign; this one warns of rocks falling from the right rock face.
[FALSE] The sign does not indicate an unpaved road; it warns of falling rocks and stones on the carriageway.
[FALSE] Danger signs never impose a numerical speed limit; a 30 km/h limit can only be set by a prohibition sign.
[TRUE] The sign (preavviso di semaforo) with three vertically arranged discs gives advance warning of traffic lights ahead.
[TRUE] Approaching traffic lights you must reduce speed so as to be able to stop if the light is red.
[TRUE] On extra-urban roads the advance traffic-light sign is mandatory.
[FALSE] A railway crossing without barriers is announced by the St. Andrew's Cross and dedicated signs, not by this traffic-light sign.
[FALSE] Alternating one-way traffic is announced by its own specific sign; this sign warns of ordinary traffic lights.
[FALSE] A movable bridge has its own danger sign; this one warns of traffic lights ahead.
[TRUE] Vehicles towing trailers (rimorchi) have a large lateral surface and reduced stability, so the danger is greater.
[TRUE] Two-wheeled vehicles are less stable, so strong side wind is more dangerous for them.
[TRUE] Vehicles towing caravans present a large side surface and are more easily destabilised by side wind.
[FALSE] The greater danger is at the tunnel EXIT, not the entrance: leaving the tunnel the vehicle is suddenly exposed to the gusts.
[FALSE] On the contrary: vehicles with trailers have worse road holding in side wind, not better.
[FALSE] Bulky loads on the roof increase the wind-catching surface and raise the centre of gravity, making the danger greater, not smaller.
[TRUE] The sign (preavviso di circolazione rotatoria) warns of an intersection of two or more extra-urban roads regulated as a roundabout.
[TRUE] It warns of a junction of several roads with rotary circulation in the direction shown by the arrows.
[TRUE] The roundabout advance sign may be used in built-up areas as well as on extra-urban roads.
[FALSE] The sign prohibits no turn; it only announces a roundabout ahead.
[FALSE] A dead-end road has its own sign; this one announces a roundabout, so there is no need to turn back.
[FALSE] A compulsory left turn is a round blue obligation sign; this one only warns of roundabout circulation.
[TRUE] The exclamation-mark sign (altri pericoli) warns of a danger for which no specific sign exists.
[TRUE] The sign warns that a danger is near and that caution is required.
[FALSE] A road in poor condition has its own specific sign; the exclamation sign covers dangers lacking a dedicated sign.
[FALSE] Proceeding straight is imposed by a round blue obligation sign; this is a generic danger warning.
[TRUE] The sign (divieto di transito, red circle with white centre) prohibits vehicle circulation in both directions.
[TRUE] The sign prohibits the transit of all vehicles (tutti i veicoli).
[TRUE] The sign is posted at both ends of the road, since the prohibition applies in both directions.
[FALSE] Bicycles are also vehicles and are prohibited; only pedestrians may pass.
[FALSE] Posted at both ends, it bans entry in both directions; the exit-only situation concerns the senso vietato sign instead.
[FALSE] One-way traffic is shown by a blue indication sign; this sign prohibits all vehicles in both directions.
[TRUE] The sign is valid 24 hours a day, including night hours.
[TRUE] The SENSO VIETATO sign is placed at the entrance of a one-way road.
[TRUE] The red disc with a white horizontal bar is the SENSO VIETATO (no entry) sign.
[FALSE] Motorcycles are not exempt; the no-entry prohibition applies to all vehicles.
[FALSE] Mopeds are not allowed to enter either; the prohibition applies to all vehicles.
[FALSE] The sign prohibits entering against the one-way direction; it has nothing to do with overtaking.
[TRUE] The no-overtaking sign allows overtaking motorcycles, which are excluded from the prohibition.
[TRUE] The no-overtaking sign can be found on both urban and extra-urban roads.
[TRUE] Overtaking between motor vehicles is forbidden even if the manoeuvre can be completed within the half-carriageway.
[FALSE] A motorcycle may not overtake a car, because cars are motor vehicles covered by the prohibition.
[FALSE] Overtaking a car is forbidden even without crossing the continuous line.
[FALSE] Overtaking between cars is prohibited regardless of whether a continuous white line exists.
[TRUE] The sign prohibits travelling less than 70 metres behind the vehicle ahead.
[TRUE] Even though two cars are depicted, the obligation also applies to motorcycles.
[TRUE] The minimum distance must be respected even when travelling at low speed.
[FALSE] The 70 metres refer to the minimum following distance, not to the start of a transit prohibition for cars.
[FALSE] The 70 is a distance in metres, not a 70 km/h speed limit.

[TRUE] A maximum speed limit sign may be found on any road, including motorways.
[TRUE] The speed limit is valid immediately after the sign itself.
[FALSE] The 80 refers to a maximum speed in km/h, not an 80-metre safety distance.

[TRUE] The sign imposes a maximum speed limit.

[TRUE] The crossed-out horn sign prohibits the use of the horn.
[TRUE] The sign prohibits acoustic signals.
[FALSE] The horn is allowed only in cases of immediate danger, not to attract attention in any circumstance.
[FALSE] Traffic congestion is not immediate danger, so the horn may not be used.

[TRUE] The sign prohibits the transit of pedestrians.

[TRUE] Only pedestrians are banned; motorcycles may pass.
[FALSE] Mopeds may pass; the sign only prohibits pedestrians.

[FALSE] The pedestrian path sign is a blue square; this red-bordered disc prohibits pedestrians.
[TRUE] The sign prohibits the transit of motorcycles.
[TRUE] Only motorcycles are banned; cars may pass.
[TRUE] The sign prohibits motorcycles of any engine capacity.
[FALSE] The sign prohibits motorcycles from passing.

[FALSE] The sign bans motorcycles from the road; it does not oblige them to use a reserved track.
[TRUE] The sign prohibits the transit of all autoveicoli (motor vehicles with 3 or more wheels).
[TRUE] Two-wheeled motorcycles are not covered by the sign and may pass.
[TRUE] Two-wheeled mopeds may pass.
[FALSE] Taxis are motor vehicles and are also prohibited.
[FALSE] Buses are autoveicoli and are prohibited.
[FALSE] Lorries are motor vehicles and are prohibited.
[TRUE] The sign is typically placed before a narrow passage (strettoia) to stop over-wide vehicles from entering.
[TRUE] The 2.30 m figure indicates the maximum width of vehicles admitted to transit.
[TRUE] The sign applies to every vehicle wider than 2.30 m, whatever its category.
[FALSE] The ban applies to all vehicles, including animal-drawn ones; anything wider than 2.30 m may not pass.

[TRUE] The sign (3.50 m with vertical arrows) shows the maximum vehicle height measured from the road surface.
[TRUE] The sign bans motor vehicles whose height, load included, exceeds 3.50 m.
[TRUE] The sign is typically placed where the road passes under a bridge, to stop over-height vehicles.
[FALSE] The sign limits vehicle height, not length.
[FALSE] Height is measured from the road surface, load included — not from the cargo bed floor.
[FALSE] The sign indicates the maximum permitted height; it has nothing to do with the safety distance from the vehicle ahead.
[TRUE] The sign (truck with 10 m) prohibits all vehicles with an overall length over 10 metres.
[TRUE] The sign bans vehicles longer than the indicated value (10 m).
[TRUE] Vehicle combinations (complessi di veicoli) are also banned when their overall length exceeds the limit.
[FALSE] The limit applies to all vehicles, including buses and vehicle combinations, not only goods vehicles.
[FALSE] 10 m is the maximum permitted vehicle length, not a distance to keep from the vehicle behind.

[TRUE] This is the 'via libera' sign: it marks the end of the prescriptions previously imposed.
[TRUE] The white disc crossed by a black diagonal band is the 'via libera' (end of restrictions) sign.
[TRUE] The previously indicated prescriptions stop being valid from the point where the sign is placed.
[FALSE] The sign applies to all vehicles, not only public service vehicles.
[FALSE] The end of a built-up area has its own sign; this one ends previously imposed prescriptions.
[FALSE] The sign ends prohibitions/obligations (prescrizioni), not danger warnings.
[TRUE] The sign indicates the end of the 50 km/h maximum speed limit.
[TRUE] Beyond the sign the 50 km/h limit no longer applies, so higher speeds within the general limits for that road are allowed.
[TRUE] The sign only cancels the maximum limit; driving below 50 km/h remains perfectly allowed.
[FALSE] It is not a speed limit sign; it marks the end of the 50 km/h limit.
[FALSE] The sign ends the 50 km/h limit; it does not prohibit exceeding 50 km/h.
[FALSE] The sign has nothing to do with safety distance; it ends the 50 km/h speed limit.
[TRUE] The sign shown is the end-of-overtaking-prohibition sign (fine del divieto di sorpasso): it marks the end of the previously imposed overtaking ban.
[TRUE] The sign marks the exact point where the overtaking prohibition ceases to apply.
[TRUE] This end-of-prohibition sign can be placed both in urban centres and on extra-urban roads.
[FALSE] It ends the overtaking prohibition; the end of a maximum speed limit is shown by a different sign bearing the speed figure.
[FALSE] The obligation to keep the safety distance always applies; the sign only ends the overtaking ban.
[FALSE] The sign ends the overtaking prohibition; it does not concern parking in a second row.
[TRUE] The sign shown is the no-parking sign (divieto di sosta), placed where parking is prohibited.
[TRUE] On urban roads, unless otherwise indicated, the sign prohibits parking from 8.00 to 20.00; on extra-urban roads the ban is permanent.
[TRUE] The sign can be supplemented by panels indicating its beginning, continuation or end.
[FALSE] It is the actual no-parking sign, not an advance warning of a no-stopping prohibition.
[FALSE] The prohibition applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles and mopeds.
[FALSE] Forced removal is not automatic; it applies only when the sign is supplemented by the zona rimozione coatta panel.
[TRUE] The no-parking sign prohibits parking (sosta) but does not prohibit brief stops (fermata).

[TRUE] The no-parking sign applies only to the side of the road where it is placed.
[FALSE] On extra-urban roads the prohibition is permanent (24 h), so parking is not allowed after 20.00 either.
[FALSE] The sign prohibits parking for all vehicles; it does not reserve parking for two-wheelers.
[FALSE] Motor quadricycles are also subject to the parking prohibition.

[FALSE] Stopping is prohibited outright, even if the vehicle would not obstruct traffic.
[TRUE] The no-stopping sign applies 24 hours a day, day and night, also in built-up areas, and therefore also prohibits parking.
[TRUE] The sign prohibits stopping for all vehicles, taxis and buses included.

[FALSE] The no-stopping sign prohibits both stopping and parking; neither is allowed.

[FALSE] The sign prohibits any voluntary stop, including stopping to let passengers get on or off.

[FALSE] The passo carrabile sign can also be placed on extra-urban roads, not only on urban ones.
[FALSE] The sign is valid 24 hours a day, not only during daytime hours.
[FALSE] The sign is valid 24 hours a day, not only during night-time hours.

[TRUE] The friction linings (guarnizioni di attrito) directly absorb the heat generated by friction and are the parts most stressed by high temperatures.

[FALSE] The vacuum servo needs the vacuum produced by the running engine; with the engine off it does not work, key inserted or not.

[FALSE] On most vehicles the steering wheel can be adjusted in rake (height) and reach to suit the driver's stature.
